plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where disorder-induced renormalization of the apparent activation scale vanishes, so the effective barrier becomes temperature independent and equal to Delta.
plan.gap_statement: The current model idealizes the disordered solid by collapsing the full distribution of hopping barriers into one temperature-independent activation energy, forcing strictly Arrhenius behavior over all sampled temperatures.
plan.baseline_assumption: A single effective activation scale represents the disorder landscape.
plan.scientific_mechanism: In a disordered insulator, thermally assisted hopping samples different subsets of localized-state pathways as temperature changes, so the apparent activation energy can vary with temperature even when the characteristic barrier parameter Delta is held fixed.
plan.rationale: The parent maps inputs through one shared Arrhenius factor controlled only by Delta/T: increasing T always reduces the exponent with a fixed slope in 1/T for each Delta, and increasing Delta rescales that slope linearly. Here the experimentally varied quantities are T and Delta, while carrier density, geometry, and disorder statistics are held fixed. A realistic next refinement is to relax the single-barrier assumption already present, not to add a separate conduction channel. In disordered hopping systems, a broad landscape of localized energies can make the apparent activation scale temperature dependent, creating curvature in ln(sigma) versus 1/T. This changes the scored target mapping itself, because sigma(T,Delta) no longer follows one separable Arrhenius form with a single shared parameter set. A single refitted parent cannot reproduce both low-T and high-T slopes across the same Delta values if the data show consistent non-Arrhenius bending. The contrast is admissible when the temperature window is broad enough to probe different effective hopping subsets; if the sampled range is narrow, the refinement may be weak and the parent may remain an adequate local approximation.

diagnostic_groups.role: fraction measuring how strongly the nominal barrier still dominates over thermal energy

diagnostic_groups.name: barrier_vs_disorder
diagnostic_groups.role: dimensionless barrier scale relative to the disorder-renormalization temperature scale, useful for detecting barrier-dependent softening efficiency

contract.activation_condition: Observable when Delta spans a range comparable to and larger than k_B*T_dis and temperatures also reach intermediate theta = k_B*T/Delta ~ 0.1 to 1, where disorder softening is active but not fully saturated.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, different Delta slices can already show unequal curvature of log(sigma) versus 1/T at similar theta; in holdout, the same mechanism extends this contrast to larger Delta where the softening suppression becomes stronger.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent when the added barrier-scale dependence vanishes, e.g. in the limit of zero strength for the new dependence or when Delta is small compared with its new crossover scale so the extra factor is effectively unity.
contract.domain_mechanism: Barrier-dependent suppression of disorder softening in hopping transport
contract.scientific_mechanism: Barrier-selective percolative filtering can become less effective for deeper localized states because accessible alternative paths remain energetically too costly, so the disorder-induced reduction of apparent activation energy depends on absolute Delta as well as on k_B*T/Delta.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the coefficient of the existing disorder-softening process now varies with Delta, changing the curvature of the scored mapping across Delta slices rather than merely rescaling conductivity or shifting one common crossover.
contract.assumption_before: A single universal temperature-crossover shape controls disorder softening for all barriers once expressed through k_B*T/Delta.
contract.assumption_after: The disorder-softening coefficient itself weakens with increasing absolute barrier scale through a barrier-filtering factor.
contract.before_fragment: sigma0*exp(-Delta/(k_B*(T + T_dis*(Delta/(Delta + k_B*T))**2/((1 + beta_shape*(k_B*T/Delta))*(1 + gamma_cross*(k_B*T/Delta)/(1 + k_B*T/Delta))))))
contract.after_fragment: sigma0*exp(-Delta/(k_B*(T + T_dis*(Delta/(Delta + k_B*T))**2/(((1 + beta_shape*(k_B*T/Delta))*(1 + gamma_cross*(k_B*T/Delta)/(1 + k_B*T/Delta)))*(1 + eta_barrier*Delta/(Delta + Delta_filter))))))
contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when eta_barrier -> 0, or approximately for Delta << Delta_filter.
contract.observable_signature: At fixed theta = k_B*T/Delta in the active regime, increasing Delta now specifically suppresses the disorder-softening contribution, so log(sigma) versus 1/T becomes less curved for large-Delta samples than for small-Delta samples; this alters the target mapping sigma(T,Delta), not merely an auxiliary interpretation.
contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting the parent's existing parameters cannot reproduce this contrast with a single shared parameter set because beta_shape and gamma_cross only reshape the common theta-dependent crossover, while T_dis sets one global softening scale. None of them introduces a separate monotone dependence of softening efficiency on absolute Delta at fixed theta, so unequal curvature across Delta slices is structurally unavailable in the parent.

range_suggestions.Delta_filter: positive, typically comparable to k_B*T_dis or the sampled Delta range
